tone_patterns: Formal, risk-management oriented tone that frames climate topics as financial and operational considerations
Uses precise definitional language before moving into implications and examples
Balances forward-looking statements (planned phases, future integration) with descriptions of current practices
Employs cautious modality (e.g., potential, could, may) when describing impacts and uncertainties
Maintains an analytical, explanatory voice rather than promotional language
paragraph_patterns: Opens with a high-level statement of recognition/importance, then immediately defines key terms used in the section
Definition blocks are followed by short illustrative examples to make abstract risks tangible
Uses region/context framing to explain why certain risks are more salient, then lists major hazard categories
Introduces a conceptual relationship (e.g., interaction of factors) and then presents an implementation roadmap
Transitions from physical risk discussion to transition risk discussion using a clear term definition and drivers list
Policy implementation paragraph structure: what was implemented, scope of applicability, and what it covers
Materiality/scenario analysis paragraphs: purpose statement, then enumerated key components, then linkage to planning
Describes analytical work in a sequence: scope selection, time horizons, inputs/scenarios, then how results are used now vs later
Uses short sub-section labels (numbered items) to segment multiple initiatives within the strategy narrative
heading_patterns: Section header repeated at the top of consecutive pages for continuity
Subheadings used as categorical labels (e.g., physical vs transition) to structure the narrative
Numbered subheadings used to introduce discrete strategic activities (e.g., stress testing, emissions tracking)
Figure titles include a figure number and a descriptive caption that states the purpose of the visual
table_patterns: Matrix-style table that maps risk drivers/topics to business impacts and organisational areas
Columns follow a consistent logic: category/driver, item and sub-items, affected areas/functions, and time horizon
Uses bullet-like entries within cells to list multiple sub-items under a single row heading
Time horizon expressed qualitatively (short/medium/long term) rather than only numeric years within the table
Table is introduced by a lead-in sentence that explains how it supports the narrative (e.g., identifies potential impacts)
figure_or_diagram_patterns: Figure used to summarise complex narrative into a structured overview (e.g., impacts across business/value chain)
Figure caption explicitly states what the figure represents (potential impacts) and ties back to preceding analysis
Visual content complements the text by consolidating categories and time horizons into a single reference point
pdf_layout_patterns: Page header/footer system includes section name and page number for navigation
Two-page spread behavior: narrative-heavy page followed by a page with structured elements (lists, mini-diagrams, or tables)
Use of whitespace and line breaks to separate definition text from examples and from bullet lists
Bulleted lists are vertically spaced and aligned for readability; long bullets wrap with consistent indentation
Small callout-style labels (e.g., category tags) appear near the bottom of a page to reinforce section structure
Figure/table placed after a short bridging sentence and before the next sub-section to act as a narrative pivot
disclosure_language_patterns: Defines key risk terms explicitly before using them throughout the section
States scope and applicability of policies/processes (entities, operations, segments) in a single consolidated sentence
Describes methodologies at a high level (scenario analysis, materiality assessment) without excessive technical detail
Connects assessments to governance/decision mechanisms (risk appetite, capital allocation, business planning) using linkage language
Distinguishes between current use of outputs and planned future integration into models/processes
evidence_presentation_patterns: Evidence is presented as process evidence (implemented policy, established assessment, conducted analysis) rather than outcome claims
Uses structured lists (numbered components) to evidence completeness of an assessment framework
Specifies analytical dimensions as evidence of rigor: scope definition, portfolio coverage, time horizons, scenario inputs
Uses a summarising figure/table to evidence consolidation of findings into decision-relevant categories
Separates qualitative findings (potential impacts) from methodological steps (how assessed) to avoid conflating inference with results
section_specific_observations: Strategy section blends narrative explanation of risk concepts with operationalisation steps (phased implementation, policy rollout)
Physical risk content is organised from definition → regional susceptibility context → hazard list → measurement roadmap
Transition risk content is organised from definition → drivers list → assessment approach → integration into planning and risk processes
The section uses both qualitative time horizons (short/medium/long) and scenario/time-horizon framing to support forward-looking analysis
things_to_avoid_copying: Any company name, branded policy name/acronym, or references to specific regulators/standard-setters
Any region-specific framing, geographic references, or asset/location descriptors
Any numeric quantities (e.g., customer counts, years, page references) and any sector-specific examples tied to the reference entity
Any claims about actions taken (e.g., financing cessation decisions) or specific portfolio decisions
Any references to specific scenario providers, supervisory bodies, or proprietary frameworks
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: References to specific regulators and scenario sources
Specific portfolio scope descriptors (e.g., top-N customers) and any numeric time horizons/years
Specific sector examples and financing decisions
Figure numbering and any table row content that could be interpreted as company-specific
